title: Acme Health - SOC2/ISO Posture Review
summary: Redwood and Acme Health review SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture, access to trust center, controls mapping, SSO/RBAC, audit logs retention and KMS integration. Customer validating hosted vs private deployment options for PHI workloads and requesting artifacts and a deeper technical session to map controls to their internal audit checklist.
topics: Data residency and private deployment options
Next steps for pilot / technical deep dive
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll get started. I know this is the SOC 2 / ISO posture review for Acme Health, thanks Lina, Mark, Priya for taking the time.
[00:08] Lina (Customer - CISO): Thanks Alex, appreciate it. We got your calendar invite. We've been through the high level security docs but need to validate specific controls and artifacts for our external auditors.
[00:15] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi all, Samir here. I'll walk through the technical controls mapping, then we can dive into SSO, audit logs, and KMS. Quick note: transcription might be a bit off, so apologies if product names get weird.
[00:25] Mark (Customer - IT Manager): No problem. We have two threads: compliance artifacts (reports, certs) and integration controls - SSO, logs, data residency. Also curious about hosted vs private for PHI.
[00:35] Alex: Great. First question for Lina — what's your audit timeline? Are you trying to compile a binder for an external auditor next month, or is this exploratory?
[00:42] Lina: External audit window Q3, so we need the SOC 2 report and an ISO controls mapping by end of July ideally. Our auditor wants to see how Redwood maps to our control objectives, evidence locations, and access to the trust center for continuous evidence.
[00:56] Alex: Understood. We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and our ISO 27001 scope documentation. We also have a Trust Center — it's the portal where we publish certs, attestation letters, penetration test summaries, and our compliance matrix. I'll share access after the call; typically we provision read-only links for customers.
[01:12] Priya (Customer - Compliance): Good. Two follow ups: 1) Is the Trust Center alignment machine-readable? Our audit tool ingests mapping spreadsheets. 2) What level of detail does the controls mapping include — do you map to AICPA COSO/CCPA or ISO controls directly?
[01:25] Samir: The Trust Center currently has downloadable PDFs and a controls mapping spreadsheet. The mapping includes SOC 2 CC criteria mapped to ISO 27001 clauses for major controls; we also provide a CSV/Excel export that auditors can ingest. It's not full automated API driven today but we can supply the matrix.
[01:40] Mark: When you say SOC 2 report, is there a redacted and non-redacted version? We need a version that shows the controls tested but not customer data.
[01:48] Alex: Yes, standard approach is redacted SOC 2 for public sharing, then under an NDA we can provide the full report. We have an NDA template we usually send as well.
[01:56] Lina: Okay helpful. Next: SSO. We run Okta. We need SAML metadata, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC controls so that our auditors can see role separation. We also need to ensure admin activities are logged with user identity tied to SSO.
[02:12] Samir: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with built-in roles and custom roles; you can scope permissions to org, project, or model. All admin and authorization events are emitted to audit logs with the SSO principal included if SSO is configured.
[02:28] Priya: How long are audit logs retained and can we extend retention? For compliance we often need 1 year plus for certain events.
[02:36] Samir: Default retention in hosted is 90 days in the console, but we support log exports to your SIEM — Splunk/Datadog/CloudWatch — and we can set up an S3 export for long term retention. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can retain on-prem and match your retention policy.
[02:51] Mark: Are logs tamper-evident? Auditors ask about integrity controls.
[02:55] Samir: We sign log bundles and include checksums for exported archives; for hosted we've got WORM-like retention options via object storage with immutability policies when requested under enterprise contracts. We'll include details in the artifact set.
[03:08] Alex: Encryption & KMS — Lina, do you have a preferred KMS? We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM-backed providers for private deployments.
[03:16] Lina: We use AWS KMS with a customer-managed key for other workloads. We need to know whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) and whether keys are stored in our account or Redwood's.
[03:25] Samir: For hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with keys we manage by default, and an option for customer-managed keys where the CMK can live in your AWS account and we use a key policy and cross-account permissions. For Private deployments you manage the KMS fully on-prem. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[03:40] Priya: What's the process for key rotation and crypto-agility?
[03:44] Samir: Key rotation is supported; for CMKs rotation is managed by your cloud KMS. For our managed keys we rotate per our crypto policy, and we publish rotation windows. We can supply the policy and rotation cadence.
[03:53] Mark: Data residency: our primary requirement is that PHI never leaves our VPC or US region. How does Redwood support region isolation?
[04:01] Alex: On Redwood Private or Dedicated, you can pin workloads to region and VPC. Hosted API is multi-region but we can restrict via customer tenancy and region selection for enterprise agreements. For PHI we typically recommend Dedicated or Private deployment so data plane never leaves your network.
[04:18] Lina: Are there third party subprocessors for hosted? We need a subprocessors list and contracts.
[04:23] Alex: Yes, we maintain a subprocessors register in the Trust Center. It includes cloud providers, analytics, and log storage providers. We can provide the list and SOC reports for critical subprocessors under NDA.
[04:34] Priya: Controls mapping — our auditor wants a row-by-row mapping to our internal control IDs. Can Redwood produce a mapping file keyed by our control IDs?
[04:42] Samir: We can create a custom mapping if you provide the control IDs and a CSV template. Typically we map Redwood controls to ISO clauses and SOC 2 criteria. For customer-specific IDs we'll work with you to fill that in; this is often part of our customer security onboarding.
[04:58] Mark: On evidence: what evidence can you provide for configuration controls? Like SSO enforcement, MFA enforcement logs, role assignment snapshots, configuration change timestamps, etc.
[05:06] Samir: We can provide snapshots and logs showing configuration states, MFA enforcement events, SCIM provisioning audit trails, and admin activity logs. Some artifacts are available via the Trust Center, others we provide as downloadable bundles for audits.
[05:20] Alex: Quick stopper question — are there any controls you currently don't meet that are commonly asked? I want to be transparent.
[05:26] Samir: We meet the core SOC 2 CC requirements and ISO 27001 controls within our scope. The biggest nuance is that hosted customers who need absolute data plane isolation for PHI are typically moved to Dedicated/Private, since multi-tenant hosted lacks physical customer separation — we manage logical segregation and controls but not physical. Most customers accept that with contractual guarantees, but some regulated customers require private deployment.
[05:46] Lina: That fits our expectation. Another line: pen tests — do you allow customer-scheduled tests or do you only publish vendor pen test results?
[05:55] Alex: We publish third-party pen test summaries. For customer-run pen tests we have a process: you sign a test authorization form, schedule a window, and we coordinate. Some customers prefer to run tests inside their Dedicated/Private environment to avoid interior traffic affecting other tenants.
[06:08] Priya: For the Trust Center access — can we create multiple read-only seats for our auditors and consultants?
[06:12] Alex: Yes, we can add org-level read-only collaborators with expiration windows. We'll send details.
[06:18] Mark: Integration question: can audit events be forwarded the moment they occur (streaming) or are they batched? Our compliance pipeline prefers near-real-time.
[06:26] Samir: We can stream events to your SIEM via Kinesis/Streaming endpoints and also provide batched daily exports. For hosted we do both; streaming may require enterprise-tier or dedicated log endpoints.
[06:38] Lina: Ok that helps. A few practical asks: 1) please send the redacted SOC 2 Type II, 2) provide the ISO scope and controls mapping spreadsheet, 3) trust center access for auditors, 4) KMS integration docs and CMK options, 5) log export and retention options documentation.
[06:56] Alex: We'll package those. I'll capture as action items.
[07:00] Samir: One more technical nuance — KV cache and prefix caching: auditors sometimes ask about stateful caches and possible data leakage between tenants. We have strict keying and zero-cross-tenant caching. We can provide the design blurb for caching and memory isolation.
[07:16] Mark: Good. Also interested in network egress controls: do you allow egress to arbitrary destinations or is it whitelisted?
[07:22] Samir: For Dedicated/Private you control egress via VPC routing and egress gateways. Hosted has outbound controls and we restrict external callbacks by config; but Dedicated gives you full network control.
[07:33] Priya: Any compliance-specific SLA or breach notification timelines?
[07:37] Alex: Our enterprise agreement includes breach notification timelines that meet standard contractual obligations — 72 hours for critical incidents, with escalation to named contacts. We'll share the contract language.
[07:47] Lina: Great. For evidence packaging, can you provide hashes and signed artifacts?
[07:51] Samir: Yes, exported bundles are signed and checksummed; we'll include verification instructions.
[07:58] Alex: Let's run through next steps quickly and assign owners.
[08:02] Mark: Sounds good.
[08:04] Alex: Action items: I'll send SOC 2 redacted and Trust Center invite; Samir will produce a controls mapping sample and KMS guide; Priya, you'll send your auditor contact and control ID CSV; Mark will coordinate SIEM for log ingestion.
[08:18] Priya: One more ques — does Redwood have a formal Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for PHI?
[08:24] Alex: We do offer a BAA for qualified customers. It's part of the enterprise contract addendum. We'll surface the BAA template after NDA if needed.
[08:33] Lina: Thanks. Last thing: Can we schedule a follow-up deep technical session to go line-by-line through our control mapping with the auditor and SE? Prefer next week.
[08:41] Samir: Yes, we can do a 60-90 minute technical deep dive — Samir and our infra specialist will join. Send preferred times.
[08:49] Alex: Awesome. Thanks everyone. I'll send notes and the artifact pack by EOD tomorrow.
[08:55] Mark: Thanks Alex.
[08:57] Lina: Thanks, bye.
[48:00] (call ends)

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and label slippage, some product names abbreviated.

Share redacted SOC 2 and ISO artifacts under existing NDA
